$comment: The one source for the communication rules. scripts/build.js renders rules/full.md and rules/condensed.md from it and generates styles/JustSaySo/ from the rules that carry a `style` block; a test fails when any of the three drift. Each rule has an id, the `full` text, an optional `short` text for the condensed reminder, and `vale`: the Vale rules that check it (an empty list is a judgment rule nothing lints). `condensed` lists the ids in reminder order. A term with `checkedBy` is listed in the text but left out of the generated style, because the named bundled rule already reports it; the bullet's `vale` list names that rule.
title: Communication rules
intro: Apply to all prose: chat, explanations, docs, reports, answers.

rules.full: Use the correct technical term when it is the most accurate word. Never substitute a vaguer word for a precise one.
rules.short: Use the correct technical term when it is the most accurate word. Never substitute a vaguer word for a precise one.

rules.full: On first use of a term the reader may not know, add a short definition in the same sentence. Then use the term freely.

The test: a technical term has a precise, checkable definition in its domain (idempotent, amortized, TLS). A buzzword could appear in any press release (robust, seamless). Keep the first kind, delete the second.
Do not remove information the reader needs. Remove information they do not need. Simplify the sentence, not the substance.
rules.short: Do not remove information the reader needs. Remove information they do not need. Simplify the sentence, not the substance.

rules.full: Claims you can check. Do not write "the only way", "handles all edge cases", or "every concern is addressed" unless you checked every case. Say which cases you checked.
rules.short: Do not claim "the only way" or "every case" unless you checked every case. Say which cases you checked.

sections.title: Sentence and paragraph mechanics
sections.note:
These are adapted from ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English), minus its 900-word approved
dictionary and minus its part-of-speech restrictions.

rules.full: Lead with the answer, decision, result, or required action.
rules.short: Lead with the answer, decision, result, or required action.

rules.full: Use descriptive headings and lists when they make longer text easier to scan.
One idea per sentence. Most sentences under 20 words.
rules.short: One idea per sentence. Most sentences under 20 words.

rules.full: Prefer active voice with a named actor (for example: "the scheduler retries the job," not "the job is retried"). Use passive voice when the actor is unknown or irrelevant.
rules.short: Prefer active voice with a named actor. Use passive voice when the actor is unknown or irrelevant.

rules.full: Prefer simple tenses (for example: "we updated," not "has been updated") when they preserve the intended time and state.
rules.short: Prefer simple tenses when they preserve the intended time and state.

rules.full: Use one term for each concept. Do not use that term for a different concept in the same document. Pick one of check/verify/validate for a given concept and keep it.
rules.short: Use one term for each concept. Do not use that term for a different concept in the same document.

rules.full: Concrete verbs and nouns over abstractions.
rules.short: Concrete verbs and nouns over abstractions.

rules.full: Noun clusters: three words maximum. Write "the retry policy for the claim adjudication engine," not "claim adjudication engine retry policy configuration."
rules.short: Noun clusters: three words maximum.

rules.full: Give each paragraph one topic. Keep most paragraphs under six sentences.
rules.short: Give each paragraph one topic.

rules.full: Keep articles and relative pronouns. Write "verify that the handler returns null," not "verify handler returns null." Do not drop function words to save space.
rules.short: Keep articles and relative pronouns. Do not drop function words to save space.

rules.full: End paragraphs with a fact or an instruction, never a flourish. The last sentence of an argument is where trained habit inserts an invented metaphor, personified code ("the config lies," "the field is a trap"), or the same point restated in stronger words. If the closing sentence adds no information, delete it.
rules.short: End paragraphs with a fact, not a flourish. No invented metaphors, no personified code, no closing restatement.

rules.full: Punctuation. No em dashes. A semicolon joins two clauses only when the second has its own comma. Otherwise write two sentences. A literal `--` belongs in a code span.
rules.short: No em dashes. A semicolon joins two clauses only when the second has its own comma; otherwise write two sentences.

rules.full: These buzzwords are banned in vague or ornamental usage: {terms}. When these words have precise meaning or are relevant to the domain, use them.
rules.short: These buzzwords are banned in vague or ornamental usage: {terms}. When these words have precise meaning or are relevant to the domain, use them.

style.name: Buzzwords
style.message: Banned buzzword: '%s'. Use a precise domain term or delete it.

terms.hint: use a concrete verb: use, apply, rely on

rules.full: Any format of "it's not {x}, it's {y}".
rules.short: Banned: any format of "it's not {x}, it's {y}".

style.name: NegativeParallelism
style.message: Banned frame: '%s'. State the positive claim directly.

patterns.regex: \b(?:it|this|that|he|she|they|we)(?:'s|'re| is| are| was| were)(?: actually)? not (?:just |only |merely |simply )?[^.,;:!?\n]{1,80}?[,;:—–]\s*(?:it|this|that|he|she|they|we)(?:'s|'re| is| are| was| were)\b
patterns.label: "it's not {x}, it's {y}" frame

rules.full: Filler frames: {terms}.
rules.short: Banned filler frames: {terms}.

style.name: FillerFrames
style.message: Banned filler frame: '%s'. Delete it and state the point directly.

rules.full: Empty intensifiers: {terms}. Replace them with a measurement or a concrete consequence.
rules.short: Empty intensifiers: {terms}. Replace them with a measurement or a concrete consequence.

style.name: Intensifiers
style.message: Empty intensifier: '%s'. Replace it with a measurement or a concrete consequence.

rules.full: Restating the question, re-summarizing what was just said, or repeating a point in new words.
rules.short: Restating the question, re-summarizing what was just said, or repeating a point in new words.

rules.full: Banned hedge frames: "It's important to note," "This may seem X, but," stacked hedges. Bare may/might/could are allowed when they state real uncertainty or permission. If uncertain, state what is uncertain and why.
rules.short: Banned hedge frames ("It's important to note," "This may seem X, but," stacked hedges). Bare may/might/could are allowed for real uncertainty or permission. If uncertain, state what is uncertain and why.

rules.full: Delete any sentence whose removal loses nothing. Check the last sentence of each paragraph first, where flourish concentrates.
rules.short: Delete any sentence whose removal loses nothing.
